newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE SHARES FALL ON PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE SHARES FALL ON PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares fell 2.7 percent on Thursday as selling pressure set in, breaking the market's month-long bull-run.

The key industrial index slid 194.41 points to close at 6,942.88, dragged down mainly by sugar refinery ZSR's 300-cent slide to 1,100 and 50-cent falls on pork processor Colcom and tyre manufacturer NTS to 290 and 500 respectively.

But brokers maintained the market was just taking a temporary breather and would pick up again as expectations of cuts in interest rates were high following a dramatic fall in annual inflation to a three-year low of 17.7 percent in August from 22 percent in July.
"This (selling pressure) should be short-lived and the market will pick up again," one broker said.

Also among Thursday's losers, packaging firm Hunyani dropped 30 cents to 360, hotel chain Zimsun shed 25 cents to 400 while Alloys at 900, tobacco company TSL at 500 and multi-industrial group Tedco at 450 all lost 20 cents.
Finance house UDC, seed firm SeedCo, timber producer EHPL and transport group Clan each slipped 10 cents to 210, 170, 210 and 170 respectively.

A handful of counters bucked the trend, notably chemical group Chemco which surged 175 cents to 1,075, cable manufacturer BICAF which rose 55 cents up to 480 and publishers Zimpapers which traded 50 cents up at 1,350.
Minings were quieter on an unmoving gold price on international markets. Wankie Colliery was the day's only winner, firming five cents to 355 while nickel giant Bindura dropped 50 cents to 1,200.
The mining index edged 3.47 points lower to end at 1,370.50.
